newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ ManFed urges no compromise on key economic policies.
newsitem.headline: NZ ManFed urges no compromise on key economic policies.

text.p: The New Zealand Manufacturers Federation on Sunday urged parties not to compromise key economic policies in the scramble to form coalitions after Saturday's indecisive general election.
"Parties have no mandate to water these policies down just to satisfy a coalition partner," ManFed Chief Executive Simon Arnold said in a statement.
"We do not expect to see policies with only minority support within the full parliament passed into law because a party gives away its pre-election promises just to get into government," he added.
Arnold said the key policies needed for continued success were:
-- A flexible employment relations system (supported by National, New Zealand First, Act and the United Party, or 60 percent of parliament)
-- No further tariffs or barriers to trade and investment (supported by National, Labour, Act, United, or 75 percent)
-- Reducing overall level of taxes (National, NZ First, Act, United or 60 percent)
-- Maintain low inflation and retaining the Reserve Bank Act (National, Labour, Act, United or 75 percent).
